claim: Tumors may be infiltrated with diffuse B cells of extra-tumoral origin or may develop organized lymphoid structures, where somatic hypermutation and antigen-driven selection occur locally.
source: The current understanding of humoral immune response in cancer patients suggests that tumors may be infiltrated with diffuse B cells of extra-tumoral origin or may develop organized lymphoid structures, where somatic hypermutation and antigen-driven selection occur locally.
evidence: This is a statement about current understanding in the field, drawing from established scientific knowledge.

claim: Draining lymph nodes are differentially involved in the interaction with the tumor site.
source: We demonstrated that draining LNs are differentially involved in the interaction with the tumor site, and that significant heterogeneity exists even between different parts of a single lymph node (LN).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing differential overlap between different LNs and tumors.

claim: Significant heterogeneity exists even between different parts of a single lymph node.
source: We demonstrated that draining LNs are differentially involved in the interaction with the tumor site, and that significant heterogeneity exists even between different parts of a single lymph node (LN).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing differences in BCR repertoire overlap between different fragments of the same lymph node.

claim: Tumor-expanded BCR clonotypes are less hypermutated than non-expanded (ubiquitous) clonotypes.
source: We identified B cell receptor (BCR) clonotypes that were expanded in tumors relative to draining LNs and blood and observed that these tumor-expanded clonotypes were less hypermutated than non-expanded (ubiquitous) clonotypes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing mutation levels between expanded and non-expanded clonotypes.

claim: There is a shift in CDR-H3 properties towards less mature and less specific BCR repertoire in tumor-infiltrating B-cells compared to circulating B-cells.
source: Furthermore, we observed a shift in the properties of complementarity-determining region 3 of the BCR heavy chain (CDR-H3) towards less mature and less specific BCR repertoire in tumor-infiltrating B-cells compared to circulating B-cells, which may indicate less stringent control for antibody-producing B cell development in tumor microenvironment (TME).
evidence: This is supported by data on CDR-H3 physicochemical properties comparing tumor and PBMC samples.

claim: B-cells may be selected according to their CDR-H3 physicochemical properties before they activate somatic hypermutation.
source: In addition, we found repertoire-level evidence that B-cells may be selected according to their CDR-H3 physicochemical properties before they activate somatic hypermutation (SHM).
evidence: This is based on analysis showing differences in CDR-H3 properties between clonotypes that belong to clonal lineages versus those that do not.

claim: In human tumors, infiltration with B-cells is often a positive prognostic factor, especially in conjunction with the formation of tertiary lymphoid structures.
source: In human tumors, infiltration with B-cells, as cells and T-cells is often a positive prognostic factor, especially in conjunction with the formation of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSss).
evidence: This is a statement about established findings in the field, drawing from scientific knowledge.

claim: Tumor-infiltrating B-cells may act via presentation of BCR-cognate antigens to T-cells.
source: Mechanistically, tumor-infiltrating B-cells (TI-Bs) may act via presentation of BCR-cognate antigens to T-cells (Zhu et al., 2015; Bruno et al., 2017; Nielsen et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Tumor-infiltrating B-cells may produce pro- or anti-tumor cytokines.
source: Mechanistically, tumor-infiltrating B-cells (TI-Bs) may act via presentation of BCR-cognate antigens to T-cells (Zhu et al., 2015; Bruno et al., 2017; Nielsen et al., 2012), production of pro- or anti-tumor cytokines Somasundaram et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2013; Ammirante et al., 2010; Pylayeva-Gupta et al., 2016
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Tumor-infiltrating B-cells may produce antibodies that are tumor-specific.
source: and production of antibodies, which may be tumor-specific DeFalco et al., 2018
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Tumor-specific antibodies may enhance killing of tumor cells via antibody-dependent cytotoxicity (ADCC).
source: and enhance killing of tumor cells via antibody-dependent cytotoxicity (ADCC) Kurai et al., 2007
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Tumor-specific antibodies may enhance antigen-presentation by dendritic cells.
source: enhance antigen-presentation by dendritic cells Carmi et al., 2015
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Tumor-specific antibodies may form immune complexes that promote the activation of myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSC).
source: or form immune complexes that promote the activation of myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSC) (Barbera-Guillem et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The effector functions of antibodies are highly dependent on antibody isotype and specificity.
source: The effector functions of antibodies are highly dependent on antibody isotype de Taeye et al., 2020 and specificity.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research and represents established knowledge.

claim: IgG1 is the most efficient factor in ADCC.
source: For instance, IgG1 is the most efficient factor in ADCC, and IgG3 (together with IgG1) is capable of complement-dependent cytotoxicity (Vidarsson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: IgG3 (together with IgG1) is capable of complement-dependent cytotoxicity.
source: For instance, IgG1 is the most efficient factor in ADCC, and IgG3 (together with IgG1) is capable of complement-dependent cytotoxicity (Vidarsson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The ability of an antibody to bind its cognate antigen increases during B-cell maturation and somatic hypermutation.
source: These functions depend on the ability of an antibody to bind its cognate antigen, which increases during B-cell maturation and somatic hypermutation (Clarke et al., 1985).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research and represents established knowledge.

claim: Isotype switching, SHM, and B-cell proliferation and differentiation are influenced by the tumor microenvironment, neoantigen burden, and presence of certain driver mutations.
source: Isotype switching, SHM, and B-cell proliferation and differentiation are influenced by the tumor microenvironment, neoantigen burden, and presence of certain driver mutations (Isaeva et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: High intratumoral immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGH) expression is strongly correlated with higher overall survival in melanoma.
source: Specifically, high intratumoral immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGH) expression, high IGH clonality, and a high proportion of IgG1 among all IGH transcripts were strongly correlated with higher overall survival in melanoma (Bolotin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: High IGH clonality is strongly correlated with higher overall survival in melanoma.
source: Specifically, high intratumoral immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGH) expression, high IGH clonality, and a high proportion of IgG1 among all IGH transcripts were strongly correlated with higher overall survival in melanoma (Bolotin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: A high proportion of IgG1 among all IGH transcripts is strongly correlated with higher overall survival in melanoma.
source: Specifically, high intratumoral immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGH) expression, high IGH clonality, and a high proportion of IgG1 among all IGH transcripts were strongly correlated with higher overall survival in melanoma (Bolotin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: High IgG1 mRNA levels are positively associated with improved prognosis in early breast cancer.
source: Similarly, high IgG1 mRNA levels are positively associated with improved prognosis in early breast cancer (Larsson et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: A high intratumoral IgG1 to IgA ratio is associated with improved overall survival in bladder cancer.
source: A high intratumoral IgG1 to IgA ratio was associated with improved overall survival in bladder cancer Dyugay et al., 2022
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: A high intratumoral IgG1 to IgA ratio is associated with improved overall survival for KRASmut but not KRASwt lung adenocarcinoma.
source: and for KRASmut but not KRASwt lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), suggesting the first link between driver mutation and B-cell response (Isaeva et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: In lung adenocarcinoma, breast cancer, and bladder cancer, only a subset of V-segments is associated with improved survival.
source: In lung adenocarcinoma, breast cancer, and bladder cancer, only a subset of V-segments is associated with improved survival (Iglesia et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The co-occurrence of specific antibody motifs and mutated tumor-derived peptides is correlated with longer survival in colorectal cancer.
source: The co-occurrence of specific antibody motifs and mutated tumor-derived peptides, presumably indicating specificity to particular tumor neoantigens, was also correlated with longer survival in colorectal cancer (Cha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: In melanoma, 30–80% of the total BCR repertoire may constitute one or several dominant B cell clones.
source: For instance, in melanoma 30–80% of the total BCR repertoire (Bolotin et al., 2017) may constitute one or several dominant B cell clones.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Some individual IGHV-genes and subgroups have been associated with autoimmunity.
source: Some individual IGHV-genes and subgroups have been associated with autoimmunity (Matsuda et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: An increase in the BCR clonal expansion index, dominated by IgA and IgM isotypes, is associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and Crohn's disease.
source: Likewise, an increase in the BCR clonal expansion index (Bashford-Rogers et al., 2013), dominated by IgA and IgM isotypes, was associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and Crohn's disease (Bashford-Rogers et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Bulk BCR repertoires are dominated by clonotypes derived from plasma cells.
source: Bulk BCR repertoires are dominated by clonotypes derived from plasma cells
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing sorted plasma cells with bulk samples.

claim: Plasma and plasmablast cells have as much as 500-fold higher IGH expression compared to naive and memory cells.
source: These clonotypes are expected to come from antibody-secreting plasma and plasmablast cells, which are known to have as much as 500-fold higher IGH expression compared to naive and memory cells (Tumeh et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The repertoire overlap between tissues, isotype composition, and clonal distribution found in BCR repertoires from bulk (unsorted) samples closely resembled those of sorted plasma cells.
source: We found that the repertoire overlap between tissues, isotype composition, and clonal distribution found in BCR repertoires from bulk (unsorted) samples closely resembled those of sorted plasma cells (Figure 2A, B and C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing bulk and sorted plasma cell samples, shown in Figure 2.

claim: The IgM proportion in tumors is significantly higher in sorted plasma cells than in unsorted TIL-B.
source: One notable exception was the IgM proportion in tumors, which was significantly higher in sorted plasma cells than in unsorted TIL-B (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There is a significant underrepresentation of IgM-producing plasma cells in bulk tumor BCR repertoires compared to other tissues.
source: This indicates a significant underrepresentation of IgM-producing plasma cells in bulk tumor BCR repertoires compared to other tissues, which in turn may indicate a lower expression of BCRs in tumor-infiltrating IgM +plasma cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the data comparing IgM proportions in sorted versus bulk samples.

claim: Significantly lower overlaps were observed between the IGH repertoires of peripheral blood and tumors compared to LN/tumor overlaps.
source: As expected, significantly lower overlaps were observed between the IGH repertoires of peripheral blood and tumors compared to LN/tumor overlaps.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data on repertoire overlap metrics.

claim: Tumor IGH repertoires are more similar to the repertoires of tumor-draining LNs than to those of peripheral blood.
source: This observation allows us to conclude that tumor IGH repertoires are more similar to the repertoires of tumor-draining LNs than to those of peripheral blood, both if clonotype frequency is taken into account, and when it is not.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data on repertoire overlap metrics (F2 and D metrics).

claim: The extent of clonal exchange between tumors and PBMC is significantly lower than that between tumors and draining LNs.
source: Overall, these analyses revealed that the extent of clonal exchange between tumors and PBMC was significantly lower than that between tumors and draining LNs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data on repertoire overlap.

claim: The frequencies of overlapping clonotypes are more strongly correlated between tumors and draining LNs than between tumors and peripheral blood.
source: The frequencies of overlapping clonotypes were also more strongly correlated between tumors and draining LNs than between tumors and peripheral blood (Fig. S1A, R metric).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure.

claim: LN/tumor overlap is higher in the IgG repertoire than in the IgA repertoire.
source: LN/tumor overlap was higher in the IgG repertoire (Figure 3E), whereas PBMC/tumor overlap was lower in the IgG repertoire (Figure 3F) than in the IgA repertoire.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: PBMC/tumor overlap is lower in the IgG repertoire than in the IgA repertoire.
source: LN/tumor overlap was higher in the IgG repertoire (Figure 3E), whereas PBMC/tumor overlap was lower in the IgG repertoire (Figure 3F) than in the IgA repertoire.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Tumor-infiltrating IgG-expressing B-cells avoid systemic circulation.
source: This suggests that tumor-infiltrating IgG-expressing B-cells (IgG-TI-Bs) avoid systemic circulation, whereas IgA-expressing tumor-infiltrating B-cells (IgA-TI-Bs) may be found in the peripheral blood with a higher probability.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential overlap patterns observed for IgG and IgA repertoires.

claim: IgA-expressing tumor-infiltrating B-cells may be found in the peripheral blood with a higher probability than IgG-expressing tumor-infiltrating B-cells.
source: This suggests that tumor-infiltrating IgG-expressing B-cells (IgG-TI-Bs) avoid systemic circulation, whereas IgA-expressing tumor-infiltrating B-cells (IgA-TI-Bs) may be found in the peripheral blood with a higher probability.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential overlap patterns observed for IgG and IgA repertoires.

claim: The tumor repertoire is significantly more clonal than the PBMC or draining LN repertoire.
source: In addition, the tumor repertoire was significantly more clonal (clonality calculated as [1-normalized Shannon-Wiener index] Tumeh et al., 2014) than the PBMC or draining LN repertoire, both overall (Figure 3C) and separately for the IGHM repertoire (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3C and 3D.

claim: In BCR repertoires from melanoma tumors, the total percentage of repertoire consisting of IgM clonotypes is significantly lower than that in other types of cancers (colorectal and lung).
source: In BCR repertoires from melanoma tumors, the total percentage of repertoire consisting of IgM clonotypes was significantly lower than that in other types of cancers (colorectal and lung; Fig. S1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure.

claim: The isotype composition of non-tumor tissues correlates with the isotype composition of the tumor.
source: The isotype composition of non-tumor tissues correlated with the isotype composition of the tumor; this effect was less prominent in peripheral blood (R=0.42, p=0.028; Figure 3G) and more prominent for LN (R=0.74, p<0.01; Figure 3H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3G and 3H.

claim: CDR-H3 length is increased in tumors compared to PBMC for the total repertoire.
source: Analysis of averaged CDR-H3 repertoire characteristics revealed increased CDR-H3 length in tumors compared to PBMC for the total repertoire (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: CDR-H3 length is increased in tumors compared to PBMC in IgA and IgG repertoires separately.
source: and also in IgA and IgG repertoires separately (Fig. S2A, B), but this was not the case for IgM (Fig. S2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: The increase in CDR-H3 length in IgA repertoires from tumor-draining LNs compared to PBMC is statistically significant.
source: In addition, the increase in CDR-H3 length in IgA repertoires from tumor-draining LNs compared to PBMC was statistically significant (Fig. S2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure.

claim: IgA CDR-H3 length is reduced in colorectal cancer, especially compared to melanoma.
source: Interestingly, the only significant difference we found when comparing CDR-H3 lengths between cancer types was reduced IgA CDR-H3 length in colorectal cancer, especially compared to melanoma (p=0.02; Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Reduced IgA CDR-H3 length in colorectal cancer could reflect a generally more mature IgA repertoire in colon tissues owing to the previous history of interactions with microbiota.
source: This could reflect a generally more mature IgA repertoire in colon tissues owing to the previous history of interactions with microbiota (Benckert et al., 2011; Hapfelmeier et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data, supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Kf4 value for the tumor repertoire is decreased compared to PBMC in the total repertoire.
source: Comparing between tissues, we found that kf4 value for the tumor repertoire was decreased compared to PBMC in the total repertoire, and kf5 was decreased in tumor vs. PBMC in the IgG repertoire (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Kf5 is decreased in tumor vs. PBMC in the IgG repertoire.
source: Comparing between tissues, we found that kf4 value for the tumor repertoire was decreased compared to PBMC in the total repertoire, and kf5 was decreased in tumor vs. PBMC in the IgG repertoire (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Kf6 value is decreased in the LN repertoire compared to PBMC.
source: In addition, kf6 value was decreased in the LN repertoire compared to PBMC.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data on CDR-H3 physicochemical properties.

claim: Kf4 inversely correlates with hydrophobicity, indicating a higher proportion of hydrophobic residues in BCR CDR-H3s from the tumor repertoire.
source: Kf4 inversely correlates with hydrophobicity, indicating a higher proportion of hydrophobic residues in BCR CDR-H3s from the tumor repertoire.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the kf4 data based on established knowledge about Kidera factors.

claim: A lower kf6 value indicates less bulky amino acid residues in CDR-H3s from the LN repertoire.
source: Kf6 is a measure of partial specific volume; therefore, a lower kf6 value indicates less bulky amino acid residues in CDR-H3s from the LN repertoire.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the kf6 data based on established knowledge about Kidera factors.

claim: The hydropathy value is lower in normal lung tissue compared to tumor, indicating a higher proportion of hydrophobic residues in tumor-derived CDR-H3 repertoires.
source: Between the tumor and normal tissue repertoires, the hydropathy value was lower in normal lung tissue, also indicating a higher proportion of hydrophobic residues in tumor-derived CDR-H3 repertoires (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: More mature B-cell subpopulations have higher mjenergy, disorder, kf4, kf6, and kf7 and lower CDR-H3 length, strength, volume, kf2, and kf3.
source: According to Grimsholm et al., 2020, more mature B-cell subpopulations have higher mjenergy, disorder, kf4, kf6, and kf7 and lower CDR-H3 length, strength, volume, kf2, and kf3.
evidence: This is a statement from a cited previous study.

claim: The mean CDR-H3 charge is negatively associated with specificity.
source: Again, the mean CDR-H3 charge was negatively associated with specificity Rabia et al., 2018
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Beta-sheet propensity is associated with antibody promiscuity.
source: and beta-sheet propensity was associated with antibody promiscuity (Laffy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Poly-reactive and self-reactive antibodies have, on average, longer CDR-H3s.
source: Poly-reactive and self-reactive antibodies have, on average, longer CDR-H3s Prigent, 2016
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Poly-reactive and self-reactive antibodies have higher charge.
source: with a higher charge Rabia et al., 2018
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Poly-reactive and self-reactive antibodies have higher net hydrophobicity.
source: and net hydrophobicity (Wardemann et al., 2003; Larimore et al., 2012; Lecerf et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The observations suggest a less mature and less specific BCR repertoire of tumor-infiltrating B cells compared to circulating B cells and B cells infiltrating normal tissue.
source: Therefore, collectively, our observations suggest a less mature and less specific BCR repertoire of tumor-infiltrating B cells compared to circulating B cells and B cells infiltrating normal tissue, which may indicate less stringent control for antibody-producing B cell development in the TME.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the CDR-H3 property data.

claim: No significant difference was found between PBMC, tumor-draining LNs, and tumors for the top 100 most frequent clonotypes in the total repertoire in terms of somatic hypermutation intensity.
source: No significant difference was found between PBMC, tumor-draining LNs, and tumors for the top 100 most frequent clonotypes in the total repertoire as well as for the top 100 most frequent clonotypes of each isotype separately (not shown).
evidence: This is based on analysis of hypermutation data.

claim: There is a statistically significant difference in the number of hypermutations in IgG between the cancers.
source: However, there was a statistically significant difference in the number of hypermutations in IgG between the cancers (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: IGHG clonotypes from lung cancer samples show higher number of hypermutations.
source: IGHG clonotypes from lung cancer samples show higher number of hypermutations, possibly reflecting high mutational load found in lung cancer tissue.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and includes a speculative interpretation.

claim: IgA-dominated clonal groups are evenly distributed among the three tissues (tumor, LN, PBMC) in all studied cancer types.
source: In all studied cancer types, IgA-dominated clonal groups were evenly distributed among the three tissues, indicating no preference for IgA-switched cells towards lymphoid or tumor tissue residence.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data on clonal group distribution.

claim: IgG-dominated clonal groups show a preference for tumor and LN residence in lung cancer and melanoma.
source: IgG-dominated clonal groups showed a preference for tumor and LN residence in lung cancer and melanoma, in accordance with the idea of tight interaction between LN and tumor in mounting anti-tumor immune responses.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data on clonal group distribution.

claim: IgM-dominated clonal groups show a strong preference for colorectal cancer tumors.
source: IgM-dominated clonal groups showed a strong preference for colorectal cancer tumors, indicating intensive intratumoral somatic hypermutation without isotype switching (Figure 5B, red triangle).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: For patient ccp2, a significantly higher overlap of tumor repertoire with one of the LNs was observed.
source: For patient ccp2, a significantly higher overlap of tumor repertoire with one of the LNs was observed (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: For ccp3, no significant difference was observed between LNs in terms of tumor repertoire overlap.
source: For ccp3, no significant difference was observed between LNs (Figure 6A, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Within a group of tumor-draining LNs, there is some inequality in terms of access to tumor antigens, and this inequality shapes the BCR repertoires within these LNs.
source: Functionally, this may again indicate that within a group of LNs, there is some inequality in terms of access to tumor antigens, and this inequality shapes the BCR repertoires within these LNs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on differential LN involvement.

claim: For lcp3, repertoire from fragment LN11 showed significantly lower overlap with the tumor than other two LN fragments, LN12 and LN13.
source: Repertoire from fragment LN11 showed significantly lower overlap with the tumor than other two LN fragments, LN12 and LN13 (Figure 7A, left).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The majority of the tumor-dominated clonal groups resided in the LN12-LN13 side of the triangle for lcp3.
source: Triangle plot analysis of clonal group distribution also showed that the majority of the tumor-dominated (red) clonal groups resided in the LN12-LN13 side of the triangle (Figure 7B, left).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The magnitude of intratumoral genetic heterogeneity correlates with the heterogeneity of immune cell infiltration.
source: Statistically, the magnitude of intratumoral genetic heterogeneity correlates with the heterogeneity of immune cell infiltration, implying the co-evolution of the tumor genetic architecture and immune microenvironment Jia et al., 2018.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Spatial heterogeneity of the T cell receptor repertoire reflects the spatial distribution of mutations in the tumor.
source: Spatial heterogeneity of the T cell receptor repertoire is also known to reflect the spatial distribution of mutations in the tumor (Reuben et al., 2017; Joshi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Higher heterogeneity of tumor-infiltrating T-cell repertoire is associated with higher risk of recurrence and shorter disease-free survival.
source: Furthermore, this is clinically relevant, because higher heterogeneity of tumor-infiltrating T-cell repertoire is associated with higher risk of recurrence and shorter disease-free survival (Reuben et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Repertoires derived from separate tumor fragments are significantly less overlapping than repertoires from biological replicates of one tumor fragment.
source: First, we confirmed for all studied tumor samples, that repertoires derived from separate tumor fragments are significantly less overlapping (F2 metric) than repertoires from biological replicates of one tumor fragment (Fig. S3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in supplementary figure.

claim: Significant patient-to-patient variability exists in the degree of heterogeneity between tumor fragments.
source: We observed significant patient-to-patient variability in the degree of heterogeneity between tumor fragments.
evidence: This is based on analysis of intratumoral BCR repertoire heterogeneity.

claim: In ccp2, all three tumor fragments had a high number of clonotypes in common and similar isotype composition dominated by IgA.
source: In a tumor from patient ccp2, all three fragments had a high number of clonotypes in common (represented also by close distance between anchor nodes on the bubble diagram), and the isotype composition was also similar and dominated by IgA (Figure 7C and D left).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 7C and 7D.

claim: IgA clonal groups are specific to ubiquitous tumor or self-antigens, whereas IgG clonal groups more likely recognize tumor specific and/or subclonal antigens.
source: This may indicate that IgA clonal groups are specific to ubiquitous tumor or self-antigens, whereas IgG clonal groups more likely recognize tumor specific and/or subclonal antigens (present only in some parts of tumor).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the clonal group distribution data.

claim: Heterogeneity plus high clonality indicate formation of TLSs and thus efficient local immune response towards tumor-related antigens.
source: Given that clonality of ccp3 tumor fragments tum_2 and tum_3 was also higher than that of ccp2 tumor, we hypothesized that heterogeneity plus high clonality indicate formation of TLSs and thus efficient local immune response towards tumor-related antigens.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed data patterns.

claim: Dense leukocytic accumulations were found frequently in the peritumoral region, as well as distant from the tumor in colorectal cancer samples.
source: We found frequent dense leukocytic accumulations in the peritumoral region, as well as distant from the tumor.
evidence: This is based on histology and immunohistochemistry analysis.

claim: Peritumoral lymphoid structures have condensed B cells follicles surrounded by T cells and high endothelial vessels (HEV), confirming that these are primary follicular TLSs.
source: Peritumoral structures have condensed B cells follicles surrounded by T cells and high endothelial vessels (HEV), confirming that these are primary follicular TLSs (Werner et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2022b).
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemistry data and supported by citations.

claim: The most expanded clonotypes in tumors were not attributed to any clonal group and were presumably not actively hypermutating.
source: Interestingly, the most expanded clonotypes were not attributed to any clonal group (and thus were presumably not actively hypermutating), and the largest of these were of IgM isotype.
evidence: This is based on analysis of expanded clonotypes and their clonal group membership.

claim: On average, expanded clonotypes had fewer mutations than non-expanded clonotypes, both in tumors and in tumor-draining LNs.
source: In addition, on average, expanded clonotypes had fewer mutations than non-expanded clonotypes, both in tumors and in tumor-draining LNs (Figure 8F, all patients).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8F.

claim: Phylogeny inferred based on short CDR-H3 sequences generally reflects the 'true' phylogeny inferred from the CDR1-FR4 repertoires.
source: The correlation was around 0.7 (p<6*10–16). Therefore, phylogeny inferred based on short CDR-H3 sequences generally reflects the 'true' phylogeny inferred from the CDR1-FR4 repertoires.
evidence: This is based on comparison of phylogenetic trees built from short and long sequences.

claim: The average distance to the root for IgM and IgA/IgG isotypes, which have significant differences for long repertoires, did not show significance for short (CDR-H3-based) repertoires.
source: However, the average distance to the root for IgM and IgA/IgG isotypes, which have significant differences for long repertoires, did not show significance for short (CDR-H3-based) repertoires (Fig. S5B).
evidence: This is based on comparison of phylogenetic analysis from short and long sequences.

claim: No correlation was found between strength, charge, and kf4 and the clonotype's position on a phylogenetic tree.
source: However, we did not find any correlation between strength, charge, and kf4 and the clonotype's position on a tree (Fig. S5C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of CDR-H3 properties along phylogenetic trees.

claim: The largest (>20 members) phylogenetic trees had dN/dS values <1, indicating negative selection pressure.
source: In addition, the largest (>20 members) trees had dN/dS values <1, indicating negative selection pressure (Fig. S5D).
evidence: This is based on analysis of dN/dS ratios in phylogenetic trees.

claim: In the absence of a defined time-controlled antigenic stimulus, in steady-state equilibrium, only a few immunoglobulin clonal groups show definitive signs of positive selection.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that, in the absence of a defined time-controlled antigenic stimulus, such as vaccination, in steady-state equilibrium, only a few immunoglobulin clonal groups show definitive signs of positive selection.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the dN/dS and CDR-H3 property data.

claim: Clonotypes not assigned to any clonal lineage (singles) had lower kf4 values, and hence higher hydrophobicity, than members of clonal groups in the tumor and PBMC repertoires.
source: In particular, clonotypes not assigned to any clonal lineage (singles) had lower kf4 values, and hence higher hydrophobicity, than members of clonal groups in the tumor and PBMC repertoires.
evidence: This is based on analysis of CDR-H3 properties depending on clonal status.

claim: The predicted interaction strength was higher for singles in PBMC and LNs, but not in the tumor.
source: The predicted interaction strength was higher for singles in PBMC and LNs, but not in the tumor, potentially indicating that tumor-resident clonotypes have undergone selection for CDR-H3 properties, irrespective of their involvement in SHM.
evidence: This is based on analysis of CDR-H3 properties depending on clonal status, with an interpretation.

claim: Clonal lineages had a higher charge in tumor repertoires, but not in the LNs or PBMCs.
source: Finally, clonal lineages had a higher charge in tumor repertoires, but not in the LNs or PBMCs, indicating a tendency towards polyreactivity in clonotypes evolving locally under the influence of TME.
evidence: This is based on analysis of CDR-H3 properties depending on clonal status, with an interpretation.

claim: Selection of CDR-H3 amino acid features occurs before cells undergo SHM.
source: These results generally match the findings of Grimsholm et al. and support the hypothesis that selection of CDR-H3 amino acid features occurs before cells undergo SHM.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on CDR-H3 properties in clonal versus non-clonal populations.

claim: The bulk RNA-based BCR repertoire is dominated by plasma cells across different peripheral compartments.
source: First, we compared BCR repertoires from PBMCs and bulk tumor infiltrates and the corresponding sorted CD19+CD20-CD38high plasma cells, and confirmed that the bulk RNA-based BCR repertoire is dominated by plasma cells across different peripheral compartments.
evidence: This is based on experimental comparison of bulk and sorted plasma cell repertoires.

claim: The overlap in BCR repertoires and the correlation of isotype proportions between tumor and lymph node samples were higher than those between tumor and peripheral blood samples.
source: The overlap in BCR repertoires and the correlation of isotype proportions between tumor and lymph node samples were higher than those between tumor and peripheral blood samples.
evidence: This is based on experimental data on repertoire overlap and isotype correlations.

claim: A higher repertoire overlap indicates a higher proportion of tumor-related BCR clonotypes in the draining LNs than in the peripheral blood.
source: A higher repertoire overlap indicates a higher proportion of tumor-related BCR clonotypes in the draining LNs than in the peripheral blood.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the repertoire overlap data.

claim: LNs are a better source of material to study anti-tumor B-cell response than PBMC.
source: Overall, LNs are a better source of material to study anti-tumor B-cell response than PBMC, and a better source of material for a potential cancer B-cell or antibody therapy, if tumor tissue is unavailable.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data on repertoire overlap and similarity.

claim: The mean CDR-H3 length of the most frequent BCR clonotypes in tumors being higher than in other tissues may indicate that tumors tend to be infiltrated with less mature B-cells compared to other compartments.
source: The mean CDR-H3 length of the most frequent BCR clonotypes in tumors was higher than in other tissues. This finding may indicate that tumors tend to be infiltrated with less mature B-cells compared to other compartments (Grimsholm et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the CDR-H3 length data, supported by a citation.

claim: Higher mean CDR-H3 length may suggest a higher proportion of autoreactive and polyreactive antibodies in tumors.
source: It may also suggest a higher proportion of autoreactive and polyreactive (Prigent, 2016; Boughter et al., 2020) antibodies, consistent with previous research.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the CDR-H3 length data, supported by citations.

claim: Lower mean CDR-H3 length in the IgA repertoire in colorectal cancer compared to melanoma may indicate that the IgA repertoire in colorectal cancer is less influenced by the TME than in other cancers.
source: However, in colorectal cancer, the mean CDR-H3 length in the IgA repertoire was lower than that in melanoma. This may indicate that the IgA repertoire in colorectal cancer is less influenced by the TME than in other cancers that we studied.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the CDR-H3 length data.

claim: Differences in CDR-H3 properties between different tissues may suggest a less mature and less specific BCR repertoire of tumor-infiltrating B-cells.
source: Differences in other CDR-H3 properties, such as mean kf3 (b-sheet preference), kf4 (inversely correlated with hydrophobicity), predicted interaction strength, and charge between different tissues, including increased central-CDR-H3 charge in the tumor compared to normal tissue, may suggest a less mature and less specific BCR repertoire of tumor-infiltrating B-cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the CDR-H3 property data.

claim: IgG-dominated clonal groups preferentially reside in tumors and draining LNs, while IgA-dominated clonal groups show a greater preference for circulation.
source: Whereas IgG clonal groups preferentially reside in tumors and draining LNs, IgA-dominated clonal groups show a greater preference for circulation.
evidence: This is based on analysis of clonal group tissue distribution.

claim: The trend for tissue preference in clonal groups reflects true clonal behavior and not simply quantitative prevalence.
source: Therefore, the trend for tissue preference reflects true clonal behavior and not simply quantitative prevalence.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the clonal group distribution data after normalization.

claim: Only draining LNs show signs of interaction with tumor antigens.
source: It is well known that only draining LNs show signs of interaction with tumor antigens (Marzo et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Within a single lymph node, individual germinal centers share their immunoglobulin clonal composition to some extent.
source: It has been previously shown that within a single lymph node, individual germinal centers (GCs) share their immunoglobulin clonal composition to some extent, and the offspring of one B-cell clone may be found in several individual germinal centers (Bende et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: During GC reactions, individual GCs become oligoclonal due to an affinity selection process.
source: During GC reactions, individual GCs become oligoclonal (containing 4–13 major B cell clones with functional IgVH, as detected in the pre-NGS era) due to an affinity selection process (Roers et al., 2000; Küppers et al., 1993; Jacob et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The BCR landscape of a lymph node remains significantly heterogeneous in space despite chronic antigen exposure.
source: We conclude that despite chronic antigen exposure, despite the ability of memory B cells to leave and re-enter germinal center reactions and form new germinal centers in subsequent rounds of affinity maturation, the BCR landscape of a lymph node remains significantly heterogeneous in space.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing spatial heterogeneity within lymph nodes.

claim: The TCR repertoire is heterogeneous in space, and this heterogeneity correlates with subclonal mutations within the tumor tissue.
source: Likewise, for tumor immune infiltrates, it was shown that the TCR repertoire is heterogeneous in space, and this heterogeneity correlates with subclonal mutations within the tumor tissue Joshi et al., 2019 and likely represents expanded mutation-specific T cell clones.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The most expanded BCR clonotypes in heterogeneous tumors rarely overlap between fragments, thus probably representing clonotypes that recognize subclonal tumor antigens.
source: In this case, the most expanded clonotypes rarely overlapped between fragments, thus probably representing clonotypes that recognize subclonal tumor antigens.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the intratumoral heterogeneity data.

claim: Clonotypes that undergo hypermutation are, on average, less hydrophobic, which indicates higher binding specificity.
source: The most prominent difference was observed for kf4 (inversely related to hydrophobicity) in PBMC and tumors; clonotypes that undergo hypermutation are, on average, less hydrophobic, which indicates higher binding specificity.
evidence: This is based on analysis of CDR-H3 properties in clonal versus non-clonal populations.

claim: The study has a limitation of a relatively short (150 bp) read length, which does not provide sufficient information for hypermutation analysis.
source: Regarding clonal lineage structure analysis, we found that our study design has a major limitation of a relatively short (150 bp) read length, which does not provide sufficient information for hypermutation analysis.
evidence: This is a self-acknowledged limitation of the study design.
